title: One line
description: A music app tab bar drawn as one continuous line. At rest you only see the icons, each a single open stroke on a 24px grid with a visible end where the thread comes in and another where it leaves: the house entered up its door post and left through a gap in the base, the magnifier entered at the handle tip with its lens left open, the heart open at its point, the books standing on one shelf line, the person drawn up through the neck, with the active one sewn in a red thread. Switching pulls the thread out of the old icon, runs it along the bar and threads it into the new one, catching the grey icons it passes; the path only appears while the thread travels it. Hold and drag and the needle comes to your finger and stays exactly under it, back and forth across the whole bar: the thread slides with you at a fixed length, unpicks the old icon as you leave and sews it back if you return, the label under the needle lights as you cross each tab, and letting go threads it into that tab. Any move can be interrupted mid-flight.
intent: Make the tab indicator a single physical thread that catches on the icons it crosses, so switching tabs reads as unpicking one icon and sewing the next.

changelog.summary:
Icons redrawn as exact Lucide glyphs (house, search, library, heart, user) on a true 24px grid with round caps and joins and consistent 2px/1px corner radii, verified by overlaying the Lucide originals
Multi-stroke glyphs (library, profile) are sewn with hidden hops where the thread passes under the fabric, so every icon lands exactly instead of as a one-stroke approximation
Stroke weight carries meaning: inactive icons 1.5px in secondary ink (1.75px on hover), the travelling thread thins under tension, and icon spans are always drawn at a full 2px with a small swell when the thread lands
Icon origins snap to device pixels on canvas and SVG alike, and the canvas DPR cap went from 2 to 3, so the landed icon is crisp at 1x, 2x and 3x
The canvas now draws straight from the track points instead of 180 resampled points, so corners and arcs in the landed icon are exact
Retargeting never reverses on itself: on the rail a reversal turns up into an upper lane, a head climbing a riser hops over in a small arch, and a half-sewn icon is left through a dive under the fabric. Velocity is carried through all three, and the drawn shape is unchanged at the moment of retarget
The zero-radius hairpin, the overlapping retrace and the instant velocity flip are gone
Dragging tracks the finger in x: vertical risers pass at up to 2.5x so the head no longer stalls coming out of an icon, the 8px axis-lock slop no longer jumps the head, and grabbing mid-flight continues the line the way it was already moving
Snag strands ease their drift direction instead of flipping when the thread reverses, and the icon the thread started from no longer snags after a mid-flight retarget
Dragging back never dead-ends: from past the last tab, mid-flight or the stub, the needle retreats to the last finished icon and leaves it the other way, or U-turns into the upper lane, instead of freezing or shrinking to a dot (0 stuck or collapsed drags across about 800 fuzzed drags at three widths, down from 16 in 300)
The finger owns the needle in x along the whole line: a monotone progress map follows x on the rail and spreads each icon's x-extent over its arc length, so the needle stays under the finger through icons, and release picks the tab under the finger rather than under a lagging head
Rollovers, folds and unwinds carry the finger's overshoot across the rebuild and settle any offset over the next 24px of travel, so the needle never jumps and never runs against the finger
Finished icons are pinned while dragging: the drag can pull back to a sewn icon's end and turn there, but never unpicks it backwards
The thread keeps at least three quarters of its rest length while dragging, so a fast pull-back no longer collapses it
A reversal that sends the thread back over its incoming rail run (dive out of a half-sewn icon, or hop off a riser) now lands on the upper lane instead of lying on top of the incoming thread
The moving thread is drawn as one filled variable-width ribbon with round end caps instead of dozens of round-capped strokes, so width seams no longer bead; landed icons stay one constant-width stroke per run
Pointer moves reuse a cached bar rect and scale instead of forcing layout on every move
The entrance animation ends on filter none, and icon snapping includes the bar's fractional page offset so canvas and SVG icons land on whole device pixels
Label weights come from the --font-weight-body-sm and --font-weight-strong tokens, and resting icons write transform none instead of keeping a 3D layer
Removed the unused firstRunLast export and the unused reverse branch of Track.appendFrom

Icons are single connected strokes again, as in the original: the house is entered and left through the open gap of its door, the library is three books joined along one shelf line, and the person is drawn up through the neck and back down, so the thread fills every gap instead of vanishing between strokes
Kept the round-one grid: Lucide house outline, magnifier and heart geometry, 24px icons, whole-unit vertical book spines that land on device pixels, and 1-unit corner radii throughout
Removed the hidden hops and the end-of-icon sink that slipped the thread under the fabric, so the moving line is never broken between an icon and the bar
Leaving a half-sewn icon is now a visible rounded drop out of the stroke onto the rail instead of an invisible dive, so the old icon and the new route stay one line
Inactive icons are one SVG path again, so the grey icon, the unpick dash and the ink thread trace exactly the same line
Drag progress no longer anchors on strokes inside a sewn icon, so dragging through the connected books spreads the stroke evenly under the finger instead of racing down the spines
Removed the now-unused under-fabric machinery: per-point hidden flags, hop weighting, per-icon unpick lengths and the separate dive floor

Every resting icon is now drawn on the canvas as one continuous grey thread: it enters each icon through the same rising lead the live thread uses, sews the connected stroke and drops back onto the rail to run on to the next, so the whole bar reads as a single line drawing instead of glyphs plus a thread
Resting icons keep the quieter ink-secondary colour and a 1.5px stroke while the leads and rail thin to 0.8px, the same tension-thinning character as the live thread
Hover, the snag tug and the unpick strand moved from the SVG to the canvas: a hovered icon darkens and thickens, a snagged icon is pulled toward the rail with its leads compressing, and the unpicked start is drawn taut from the foot of its own lead so the grey thread never breaks
The SVG icons stay in the markup as the first-paint and no-JS fallback and hide once the canvas has drawn the thread
The live thread is red by default, a refined red mixed 14% from the site red toward ink rather than the raw token
Added a hand-rolled Thread panel under the phone with colour presets (red, ink, blue accent, gold) and three weights (fine 1.5, regular 2, bold 2.5) that scale the live thread, the resting icons and the rail together; below 900px it collapses behind a Thread toggle in the header
The thread choice is saved to localStorage behind try/catch and restored through useSyncExternalStore with a server snapshot, so there is no hydration mismatch and no setState in an effect; it also syncs across open tabs
The resting line is decimated at build time to its corners and 0.15 rad curve steps, with the snag anchor inserted as an explicit vertex, which cuts its per-frame canvas calls by more than half

Removed the permanent grey line: no rail along the bar and no stems from the icons down to it, so at rest the bar is only the five glyphs and the travel path appears only while the thread moves along it
Inactive icons stay one-string thread shapes drawn as standalone glyphs on the canvas, with hover emphasis and the snag intact; the snag no longer compresses leads or anchors to the rail, the loose end just lifts a few pixels toward the passing thread and the icon eases back without wobbling
Removed the hover peek that pulled a tail out of the active icon toward the bar while resting
Dragging is finger-owned: the needle is placed by the finger x on the rail exactly (0.09px mean error, down from 11px), instead of being moved by accumulated deltas that started at the icon end and dropped the first 8px of travel
The needle no longer races through icons while dragging; it rides the rail under the finger, so the arc per pixel of finger is 1 on the rail and at most 1.57 through the corner out of the icon (was up to 6.25)
Reversals retrace the same path, and crossing back over the start icon swings the corner to the other side at the shared point under the icon, so there are no rollovers, folds, unwinds or slip offsets to settle while you drag back and forth
The thread keeps a fixed length while dragging, so the old icon unpicks and re-sews exactly in step with the finger and nothing keeps moving once you hold still
Grabbing away from the needle or mid-flight catches the needle up to the finger once, with a critically damped catch-up capped at 1200px/s, and flows through the corner without stopping when the finger is on the other side
Labels follow the needle while dragging: the tab under it lights with a short crossfade at the boundary, and release always picks that same tab instead of projecting the fling, so the label, the needle and the selection never disagree
After release the chosen label stays lit while the thread sews in and any partly lit neighbour fades in step with the sewing
Removed the drag progress map, retreat floors, rollover and fold-back rebuilds and the release velocity sampling in the bar
Home is an open stroke: the thread enters up the left door post and the left base stops 3 units short of it after rounding the corner, so the entry and exit ends sit either side of a visible gap
Search is an open stroke: the thread enters at the handle tip, runs up to the lens and loops it the other way, stopping short of the handle joint so the lens stays open there and the exit drops out of the bottom without crossing the handle
Liked is an open stroke: the two lobes no longer meet at the bottom point, so the thread enters up the right side and leaves down the left with a gap at the tip
When the needle enters an icon the icon gets tugged toward where the thread came from, down and toward the side it ran in from, then springs back with one gentle overshoot: up to 2.5px down and 1.25px sideways, damping 0.62, peak at 48ms, a single 8% overshoot at 215ms, settled by about 300ms
When the last stitch lands the icon cinches with a scale pop to 1.06 about its centre (damping 0.62, peak at 41ms, settled by about 260ms), and the label weight ticks from 590 to 600 and back in step with the pop
The icon the thread leaves gives a lighter release twitch the moment the tail clears it, 40% of the arrival tug and upward
Every reaction scales with arrival speed (full at 900px/s, never below a quarter), and a drag release is further scaled by finger speed at release, so a slow drag lands as a soft nudge (about 0.7px) and a fast tap or flick as a firm jolt (about 2.2px)
The reactions are springs on the engine clock that add to whatever is already moving, so they stay interruptible; the red thread inside an icon moves with the icon so thread and glyph never separate, and reduced motion has no reaction at all
